title: What Ecclesiastes Actually Means by Two Are Better Than One
caption:
Ecclesiastes never called alone strength. Two are better than one. He meant that literally.

If either of them falls, one can help the other up. But pity the man who falls with no one there (Ecclesiastes 4:10). If two lie down together, they will keep warm. How can one keep warm alone (4:11)? Though one may be overpowered, two can defend themselves. A cord of three strands is not quickly broken (4:12).

Two men and God between them. That's the math that holds. Solomon didn't write brotherhood in as a suggestion. He wrote it in as strategy.

Go find the second strand.
